Aleksandrow Lodzki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Aleksandrów Łódzki, Poland

Not demolished. Aleksandrów Łódzki, granted town rights in 1822, recorded its first Jews in 1818; by 1897, 1,673 (28%) supported synagogue supervision established alongside the first synagogue in 1822. In 1866, tzadik Chanoch Henich ha Kohen Lewin of Góra Kalwaria settled there, making the town a major Hasidic center; the 1870s brought Jechiel Danzigier, founder of the Aleksander dynasty - by the eve of WWII, Aleksander Hasidim formed Poland's second-largest Hasidic movement, and a brick tzaddik's mansion was built in 1935. On December 27, 1939, all approximately 4,000 local Jews were displaced to the General Government and eventually Nazi extermination camps. This cemetery, probably established around 1822, holds Chanoch Henich's grave (buried 1870) beneath a renovated concrete tomb, alongside his daughter Chaja Cipora's renewed matzevah; a separate ohel houses Jechiel Dancygier (d. 1894) and three successor Aleksander rebbes (d. 1910, 1923, 1924). On September 14, 1939, Germans shot 26 Jews and 5 Poles at the cemetery, commemorated with a Polish plaque. The site remains an active pilgrimage destination for Aleksander Hasidim; in 2010, about 400 people from around the world attended the hundredth Jahrzeit of Jerachmiel Israel Icchak Dancygier. Numerous matzevot have been recovered from town streets over the years and relocated behind the ohel.
